newsitem.title: UK: SocGen Romania fund heavily oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: SocGen Romania fund heavily oversubscribed.

text.p: Societe Generale's Emerging Europe Asset Management (SGEEAM) said on Thursday its new Romanian equity fund had been heavily oversubscribed, and it would raise the issue size to $50 million from $30 million by exercising a greenshoe option.
The book closed on the new fund on Wednesday with subscriptions totalling about $150 million, SGEEAM managing director Richard Harding told Reuters.
Harding said subscriptions had come from a broad range of financial institutions and banks from the UK, continental Europe and the U.S.

The fund, which will invest in listed and unlisted securities, will be a closed-end investment company incorporated in Guernsey. It had an initial issue size of $30 million, with a $50 million maximum.
"As central Europe's second largest market, Romania is attracting a great deal of international attention from investors," it said in a statement.
It said the new government had committed itself to a comprehensive package of social and economic reforms.

"The change in political will and the potential growth have convinced SGEEAM to establish this new fund to provide investors with the opportunity to participate in dynamic companies at an early stage of development," SocGen said.
A local asset management office has been set up.
